Date: Mon, 04 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on Redwood invoice intake (portal vs email)

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the onboarding call last week. Our finance team is working through the practical details before go-live and asked whether Redwood prefers we submit invoices via your vendor portal or continue sending them to accounts-payable@redwood.ai. We have two constraints:

- Our ERP currently spits out a compact CSV we can attach to emails if needed.
- We can use your portal but need a sample of the exact field mapping so our engineers can auto-populate the export.

I've attached a representative CSV with three sample rows (zephyr_sample_rows.csv). Could you confirm:

1) Which intake method gives the fastest payment SLA?
2) If portal, do you require PO numbers in a specific column header?
3) If email, is there a subject convention or PO-stamp requirement so your AP auto-ingests correctly?

Appreciate the quick guidance — we are targeting our first invoice the week of Aug 18.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Finance, Zephyr Systems
Attachments: zephyr_sample_rows.csv

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick question on Redwood invoice intake (portal vs email)

Lena —

Thanks for the sample CSV, that helps a lot. Quick answers up front:

- Portal generally yields the quickest processing and the cleanest matching to POs (shorter exception path). If you can hit the portal, we recommend it.
- PO placement: our portal expects a PO value in a field labeled "po_number" (we also accept "PO#" or "PO_ID" but mapping to "po_number" is preferred).
- Email fallback: if you have to email, use subject line: "Invoice: <Zephyr Invoice #> | PO:<po_number>" and attach the CSV. Put PO into the first CSV column header named "po_number" if possible.

I'm looping in Vanessa (on vendor onboarding) and Marcus (billing) so we can give a concrete minimal row schema to hand to your engineers. Vanessa / Marcus — can you review the attached sample and confirm the minimal required columns and any header-normalization rules?

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Vendor Ops Lead | Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Lena / Procurement —

Appreciate the updated CSV. Final alignment from our side:

- Recommendation: Use the portal for production invoices. It hits the short queue and preserves PO-line matching. If you go portal, we will give you a small mapping JSON (one-time) and a test tenant to push to. That path gets you to standard payment SLA.
- Email backstop: Acceptable for the first two months while you short-cycle your ERP change. For email, please:
  • Use subject format: "Invoice: <Vendor Invoice #> | PO:<po_number>"
  • Attach a CSV where the first column header is "po_number" and include a column "invoice_total". If you consolidate lines, include a column "line_count" (1 if consolidated).
  • Include PDFs as separate attachments and name them: "INV-<invoice#>-receipt.pdf" — we do ingest attachments but we prefer the CSV for automated ledgering.

- Minimal required CSV headers for our AP automation: po_number, invoice_number, invoice_date (YYYY-MM-DD), invoice_total, currency, vendor_name. Optional but helpful: invoice_line_description, invoice_line_amount, line_count.

Attached is a short policy doc with the PO-stamp rule and examples (kimberly_po-stamp-policy.pdf). We'll provision portal access by Aug 11 and send mapping details.

If you want, Marcus can run a quick sanity test on a canned CSV once you push it to the test tenant — Marcus, can you take that?

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Vendor Ops Lead | Redwood Inference
Attachments: kimberly_po-stamp-policy.pdf
